name: 99 (trick-taking)
description: Ninety-Nine: trick-taking with exact-trick bidding. Bid by discarding 3 cards (Clubs=3, Hearts=2, Spades=1, Diamonds=0). 3-4 players; 36 or 52 cards. Follow suit; score for making exact bid and premiums for face-up or revealed hand. Designed by David Parlett 1967-68.

content.text: Ninety-Nine: trick-taking with exact-trick bidding. Bid by discarding 3 cards (Clubs=3, Hearts=2, Spades=1, Diamonds=0). 3-4 players; 36 or 52 cards. Follow suit; score for making exact bid and premiums for face-up or revealed hand. Designed by David Parlett 1967-68.
Invented by David Parlett (1967-68). Trick-taking with exact-trick bidding via discard (suit = trick value). Distinct from adding game 99.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 52-card deck

Table space

items.text: Ninety-Nine for three players (standard game): Base Ninety-Nine uses a 36-card French-suited pack, deals 12 cards to each of three players, and has everyone discard three bid cards whose suits encode an exact trick target.
Ninety-Nine for four players: Four-player Ninety-Nine uses a full 52-card deck, deals 13 cards each, and allows bids up to 10 tricks, with three diamonds representing either 0 or 10 tricks.
Ninety-Nine for five players: Five-player Ninety-Nine uses a Five Hundred style pack including elevens and twelves, with each player discarding three bid cards to aim for up to nine tricks.

Two-player Ninety-Nine with dummy: In the two-player variant a third dummy hand is dealt, its three bid cards are set aside unseen, and the live players both bid and may declare while also playing cards from the dummy hand.
Original Ninety-Nine with joker: The original three-player version adds a joker to the 36-card pack, uses the turn-up card to set trumps, and plays a fixed rubber of nine deals.
Declarer chooses trumps: In this variation a player who declares or reveals also chooses the trump suit for the deal instead of using the usual success-based trump rotation.
Unbidden Ninety-Nine: Unbidden Ninety-Nine delays bidding until the final three cards of each hand, using those cards as the bid while players have already played nine tricks.
